standard.title: Changes, transitions and support
standard.description: analyse the impact of changes and transitions, and devise strategies to support themselves and others through these changes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have investigated resources and strategies to manage changes and transitions, including puberty (Y5-6). They can identify strategies and resources but have not yet been expected to analyse the impact of transitions systematically or devise strategies for supporting others.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse the impact of changes and transitions, and devise strategies to support themselves and others through these changes.

nodes.label: Understanding types of changes and transitions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the range of significant changes and transitions relevant to their age group and describe the types of impact — social, emotional, physical — each can have.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two changes or transitions relevant to their age group and describe one type of impact each can have.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of significant transitions (puberty, changing peer/family relationships, social transitions, cultural transitions) and describe their social, emotional and physical impacts; distinguish between predictable and unexpected transitions.
wider: Examine how ceremonies of First Nations Australians involve sharing of cultural knowledge and mark changes in social standing and responsibilities, comparing these transition structures to those in students' own communities
Explore the concept of 'border crossing' — how First Nations Australians navigate multiple cultural contexts — and how this type of ongoing transition can impact sense of belonging

response_modes.reason: A broad repertoire of transition types prevents students from treating only visible physical changes as significant — emotional, social and cultural transitions are equally important in this descriptor.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two changes or transitions relevant to their age group
Describes at least one type of impact (social, emotional or physical) for each identified transition

nodes.label: Analysing the impact of changes and transitions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse the specific impact of one or more transitions on individuals — including emotional, relational and identity effects — and explain what factors influence how significant the impact is.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse the impact of one transition on an individual, identifying at least two specific effects and one factor that influences how significant the impact is.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse the impact of transitions across multiple types; identify factors that mediate impact (social support, coping skills, cultural resources, individual disposition); examine how puberty-related changes affect emotional responses and relationships.
wider: Investigate how accessing and assessing health and sexual health information supports young people through puberty-related transitions, evaluating the quality and relevance of available sources

Examine the emotional and relational impacts of 'border crossing' for First Nations young people navigating multiple cultural contexts, considering how this ongoing transition intersects with other developmental changes
nodes.hinge_reason: Devising strategies requires understanding what the strategies are responding to — students who cannot analyse the impact of transitions will devise generic coping strategies unconnected to the specific experience being managed.

response_modes.reason: Scaffold impact analysis by explicitly modelling the analysis of a specific transition: what changes, for whom, in what ways, and what makes the impact greater or lesser for different people? This builds the analytical structure students need before devising strategies.

success_criteria: Analyses at least two specific effects of a named transition on an individual
Identifies at least one factor that influences how significant the impact is

nodes.label: Devising strategies for support
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can devise practical strategies to support themselves and others through specific transitions, including accessing relevant health information and services.
nodes.minimum_width: Devise at least one strategy for supporting themselves or another person through a specific transition, giving a reason why it would be effective.
nodes.typical_width: Devise a range of strategies — including coping, communication and problem-solving strategies — for supporting themselves and others through multiple transition types; access and assess health information and services relevant to managing specific transitions; evaluate and practise strategies.
wider: Evaluate and practise coping, communication and problem-solving skills for managing emotions and changes associated with puberty and getting older, comparing the effectiveness of different strategy types
Research transition support resources available to young people in their community and evaluate their accessibility and relevance for different transition scenarios

response_modes.reason: Strategy devising integrates transition impact understanding, knowledge of available resources, and practical skill application — instruction should position strategy development as responsive to analysis findings, not as a separate task.

success_criteria: Devises at least one strategy for supporting themselves or another person through a specific transition
Explains why the strategy would be effective for that transition
Identifies at least one health information source or service relevant to the transition
